quote: Adisaivas are Saivites, who have survived the absorbing influence of the Lingayat sect.
note: Census 1901: a sub-caste of Vellala; singers of Devara hymns in Saiva temples. No matha named.

quote: As the Agamudaiyans are Saivites, Pandarams assist at the funeral ceremonies.
note: Pandarams (Saiva religious mendicants/priests) assist; no matha named.

quote: The Agasas are Vishnuvaits, and pray to Vishnu, Pattalamma, and the Saktis.
note: Gurus are Satanis: 'Their gurus (religious preceptors) are Satanis.' No Ramanuja tie stated.

quote: Like many other Oriya castes, the Aliyas follow the Chaitanya form of Vaishnavism, and also worship various Takuranis (village deities).
note: Chaitanya (Paramartho) Vaishnavism.

quote: As a community the Ambattans are divided into Saivites and Vaishnavites.
note: Vaishnavite section 'branded by their Brahman guru with the chank and chakram'; intermarriage between the two sections allowed.

quote: In the Madras Census Report, 1891, the Andis are summed up as "beggars who profess the Saiva faith.
note: Tanjore Manual also: 'applied to those who profess the Saiva faith'. Andis are Saiva mendicants, no matha named.

quote: Some of them are Saivites, and others Vaishnavites.
note: Brahmans employed as priests by the Vaishnavites, not by the Saivites.

quote: Over each of these is a headman called the Periyadanakkaran, and the three former are also subject to a Guru who lives at Sirupalai near Madura.
note: Sect of the guru not stated.

quote: As might be expected, the members of this sect are staunch Saivites.
note: Brahman sect found mainly in the four northern districts; wear both sacred thread and linga; 'do not accept offerings distributed in temples'; no matha named. Thurston: 'The Aradhyas are a sect of Brahmans found mainly in the four northern districts of the Madras Presidency, and to a smaller extent in the Cuddapah and Kurnool districts.'

quote: Rajpindes are both Vishnavites and Sivites, and their priests are both Brahmans and Lingayat Waders."
note: Mysore Census quotation; also Lingayat priests for the Siva part.

quote: They wear the sacred thread, have Brahmans as their priests, and give allegiance to the head of the Sringeri Mutt.
note: H. A. Stuart: 'true Ares' found in South Canara, Bellary and Anantapur; guru's sanction needed for divorce.

quote: The Udayas, Adhikaris and Kanakas are Lingayats in religion, and the other three, the Haruvas, Badagas, and Toreyas are Saivites.
note: Udayas are priests to Lingayat Badagas; Jangam respected.

quote: The Udayas, Adhikaris and Kanakas are Lingayats in religion, and the other three, the Haruvas, Badagas, and Toreyas are Saivites.
note: Same sentence as Lingayat division row.

quote: The Badhoyis are Paramarthos, and follow the Chaitanya form of Vaishnavism.
note: Chaitanya (Paramartho).

quote: The Bagatas are both Vaishnavites and Saivites, and the former get themselves branded on the arm by a Vaishnava guru, who lives in the Godavari district.
note: Satanis officiate for Vaishnavites, Jangams for Saivites.

quote: The Bairagis are Vaishnavites, and bear the Tengalai Vaishnava mark (namam), made with sandal-paste or gopi, on the forehead.
note: Tengalai namam; Vadagalai mark very rare; guru called Mahant, some pay respects to the Mahant of Tirupati temple. Ramanand schism mentioned. Ramanuja affiliation inferred from namam.

quote: Probably they originally assumed Jainism as a fashionable addition to the ancestral demon worship, to which they all still adhere, whether they profess to be Vaishnavites, Saivites, or Jains.
note: About ten thousand Bants are Jains; rest Hindu Sudras. No matha named in the packet cue sentences.

quote: Their guru is known as Tirumalatatacharya, who is also a head of the Srivaishnava Brahmans.
note: Mysore Census 1901; Uru Bedars submit disputes to guru, a Srivaishnava Brahman; Dasari/Samaya brands (chakrankitam). Vadagalai/Tengalai not stated.

caste_std: Bedar: Myasa Bedar converts to Saivism
quote: The guru is the head of the Ujjani Lingayat matt (religious institution) in the Kudligi taluk of Bellary.
note: 'some Myasa Bedars have changed their faith, and are now Saivas ... converted by Jangams'; do not wear the lingam. Referent of 'The guru' follows the Myasa sentence; Myasa Bedars elsewhere said to have no guru.

quote: Some Beri Chettis, Mr. Stuart writes, "worship Siva, and some Vishnu, and a few are Lingayats, who do not marry into families with a different worship.
Besthas employ Brahmans and Satanis (or Jangams, if Saivites) for their domestic ceremonies, and imitate the Brahman customs
note: Telugu Besthas get branded with chank and chakram; Parigirti never are; Pakirithi = Vaishnava per Thurston.

quote: They have the Telugu Janappans as their disciples, and are the only non-Brahman caste, except Jangams and Pandarams, which performs the duties of guru or religious instructor.
note: Gurus of Janappans; sect not stated here (see vol 2 Janappan: Vaishnavite Janappans are disciples of Bhatrazus).

quote: Most of the Bhondaris follow the form of Vaishnavism inculcated by Chaithyana, and known as Paramartho matham.
note: Chaitanya.

quote: The Bolasis are Vaishnavites, and observe the Paramartho or Chaitanya form thereof.
The Sivaites of this sect are said to bury their dead, while the Vishnavaites burn.
note: Census 1891: Besides Siva and Vishnu worship, village deities.

quote: Most of the Bosantiyas are Saivites, but a few follow the Paramartho form of Vaishnavism.
note: Part Chaitanya Vaishnava.

quote: Ashtakshari (eight syllables).--A sub-division of Satanis, who believe in the efficacy of the eight syllables om-na-mo-na-ra-ya-na-ya in ensuring eternal bliss.
note: Sect not named explicitly; Vaishnava mantra.

quote: From a religious point of view, the Brahmans are either Saivites or Vaishnavites. The Saivites are either Saivites proper, or Smarthas.
note: Vaishnavites of three kinds: followers of Chaitanya, Ramanuja, Madhvacharya. Smarthas recognise the Trimurtis.

caste_std: Brahman (general): Sri Vaishnava initiation by mutt head
quote: The ceremony of initiation (samasrayanam) is usually performed by the head of a mutt.
note: General Sri Vaishnava statement; mutts then listed (see Vadagalai/Thengalai rows).

quote: All these are Smarthas, who use as their sect mark either the urdhvapundram (straight mark made with sandal paste) or the circular mark, and rarely the cross lines.
note: Sub-divisions Choladesa, Vadadesa, Savayar/Sabhayar, Inji, Thummagunta Dravida. Worship Siva and Vishnu; some use Vaishnava namam (Kiththunamakkarar); 'Vadamam muththi Vaishnavam'. No matha named.

quote: (b) Kesigal.--The Kesigals, or Hiranyakesikal (men of the silvery hair), as they are sometimes called, closely resemble the Vadamas
note: Listed by Thurston under 'I. Smartha'. No matha named.

quote: Some Smarthas, e.g., the Brahacharnams, are more Saivite than other sections of Tamil-speaking Brahmans.
note: Vibhuti, horizontal sandal lines, rudraksha, lingam; Sathyamangalam sub-division sometimes Vaishnava mark (Purattasi, Venkataramana). No matha named.

quote: (d) Vathima.--The Vathimas, or Madhimas, are most numerous in the Tanjore district
note: Listed under 'I. Smartha'. No matha named.

quote: The members thereof are, like the Brahacharnams, more Saivite than the Vadamas.
note: Listed under 'I. Smartha'. No matha named.

quote: As a class the Dikshitars are haughty, and refuse to acknowledge any of the Sankarachariars as their priests, because they are almost equal to the god Siva, who is one of them.
note: Listed by Thurston under 'I. Smartha' but explicitly reject any Sankaracharya; a Sankaracharya visiting the temple may not take ashes direct from the cup. Priests of Nataraja temple. Counter-evidence to Sankaracharya allegiance. REVIEWED Nov 2026: kept as Thurston's Smārta listing, but counts AGAINST Śaṅkarācārya allegiance (they reject any Śaṅkarācārya).

quote: They eat with the other Smartha Brahmans, but do not intermarry.
note: Temple servants; Vaishnava Sholiars also exist and are 'considered somewhat low'; intermarriage between Smartha and Vaishnavite Sholiars.

quote: (h) Mukkani.--The Mukkanis are Smarthas confined to the Cochin and Travancore States.
A large number of them, though Smarthas by birth, wear a mark on their forehead like Vyshnava Brahmins, and serve as cooks and menial servants in the big temple at Srirangam.
note: Ramachendrier quotation.

quote: It is said that some 700 years ago, about 1,000 families of Smartha Brahmans emigrated from the vicinity of Kanchi (Conjeeveram)
note: Kausika and Bettadapura Sanketis; Mysore Census 1891. No matha named.

quote: The Prathamasakis are found among all the linguistic sections. Among Smarthas, Andhras, and Vaishnavas, they are regarded as inferior.
note: Sukla Yajurvedis; listed by Thurston under 'I. Smartha'. No matha named.

quote: Gurukkals are Saivites to a greater extent than the Smarthas, and do not regard themselves as disciples of Sankaracharya.
note: Listed under 'I. Smartha' but explicitly not disciples of Sankaracharya; temple priests of Siva temples (Bodhayana sutra); Tiruvalangad, Conjeeveram, Tirukkazhukunram sub-divisions.

quote: For Vadagalais there are two mutts. Of these, the Ahobila mutt was formerly at Tiruvallur, but its head-quarters has been transferred to Narasimhapuram near Kumbakonam.
note: Vadagalai; mutt head-quarters moved from Tiruvallur to Narasimhapuram near Kumbakonam. No 'jiyar' term in the article.

quote: The Parakalaswami mutt is in the Mysore Province.
note: Vadagalai.

quote: For Thengalais there are three mutts, at Vanamamalai and Sriperumbudur in Chingleput, and Tirukoilur in South Arcot. These are called respectively the Tothadri, Ethirajajhir, and Emberumanar mutts.
note: Thengalai. Printed text places Vanamamalai in Chingleput; mutt names Tothadri (Vanamamalai), Ethirajajhir (Sriperumbudur), Emberumanar (Tirukoilur) by order of the sentence.

quote: For Thengalais there are three mutts, at Vanamamalai and Sriperumbudur in Chingleput, and Tirukoilur in South Arcot.
note: Thengalai; mutt called Ethirajajhir (Yatiraja) in the text.

quote: For Thengalais there are three mutts, at Vanamamalai and Sriperumbudur in Chingleput, and Tirukoilur in South Arcot.
note: Thengalai; mutt called Emberumanar in the text.

caste_std: Tamil Brahman: Hebbar and Mandya Vaishnava
quote: The Hebbar and Mandya sections belong to the Mysore Province, in which the former are very numerous.
note: Listed under both Vadagalai and Thengalai; speak Tamil with Carnataka marriage details. Mandyas migrated from near Tirupati.

quote: The Vaikhanasas and Pancharatras are temple priests (archakas).
note: Branding regarded as unnecessary by them; listed under Vadagalai and Thengalai; title Dikshitar. Ramanuja tie not stated.

quote: A good example of Smarthas becoming Vaishnavas is afforded by the Thummagunta Dravidas, some of whom have become Vaishnavas, but still take girls in marriage from Smartha families
note: Immigrants listed under Telugu and Vadama.

quote: the Pattars present no peculiarities distinguishing them from the ordinary East Coast Brahmans.
note: No sect or matha stated for Pattars / Arya Pattars.

quote: The Aradhyas are dealt with in a special article (see Aradhya).
note: Listed among Vaidiki sub-sections; see Aradhya entry.

quote: The Nandavariki Brahmans are, in fact, gurus or priests to the Devengas.
note: Rig Vedis; tutelary goddess Chaudeswari; sect of the Brahmans not stated.

quote: The Madhva Carnatakas are recent converts from Carnataka or Andhra Smarthas.
note: Telugu Brahman sub-divisions (Vaidiki, Niyogi, Tambala) carry no sect or matha statement; Andhra Smarthas mentioned only in passing.

quote: Some are converts from Telugu Smarthas, and are called Andhra Vaishnavas.
note: They do not mix with other Tamil-speaking Vaishnavas.

quote: Madhvas, excepting the very orthodox, will take food with both Carnataka and Andhra Smarthas.
note: Seven Smartha sub-divisions: Aruvaththuvokkalu, Badaganadu, Hosalnadu, Hoisanige, Kamme, Sirnadu, Maraka. No matha named in the list itself.

quote: The Madhva Carnatakas are recent converts from Carnataka or Andhra Smarthas.
note: Madhva sub-divisions: Aruvela, Aruvaththuvokkalu, Badaganadu, Pennaththurar, Prathamasaki, Hyderabadi.

quote: The Pennaththurars are supposed to be Tamil Brahmans converted into Madhvas.
note: Retain Tamil tali.

quote: About 25 years ago, the Sringeri Math issued on behalf of the Smarta portion of the people a Srimukh (papal bull) acknowledging them to be Brahmans.
note: Claiming Brahman status but not recognised. Descended from disciples of Sankaracharya, 'the original guru of Sringeri' (legend of toddy and red-hot iron). Mysore Census 1891.

quote: A similar pronouncement was also obtained from the Parakal Math at Mysore about three years later on behalf of the Srivaishnavas among them.
note: Also: 'some have recently become disciples of Parakalaswami.' Marakas 'chiefly Vishnuvites' (Lewis Rice).

quote: Madhvas have four mutts to which they repair for the branding ceremony, viz., Vayasaraya, Sumathendra and Mulabagal in Mysore, and Uttaraja in South Canara.
note: Printed 'Vayasaraya'. Madhvas branded each time they see the guru.

quote: Madhvas have four mutts to which they repair for the branding ceremony, viz., Vayasaraya, Sumathendra and Mulabagal in Mysore, and Uttaraja in South Canara.
note: Printed 'Sumathendra'.

quote: Madhvas have four mutts to which they repair for the branding ceremony, viz., Vayasaraya, Sumathendra and Mulabagal in Mysore, and Uttaraja in South Canara.
note: Printed 'Mulabagal'.

quote: Madhvas have four mutts to which they repair for the branding ceremony, viz., Vayasaraya, Sumathendra and Mulabagal in Mysore, and Uttaraja in South Canara.
note: Printed 'Uttaraja'; its followers branded in five places.

quote: Sankaracharya founded the Sringeri Matha in Mysore near the borders of the Udipi taluk, the guru of which is the spiritual head of such of the Tulu Brahmins of South Canara as have remained Smarthas or adherents of the teaching of Sankaracharya.
note: H. A. Stuart quotation. Thurston/Stuart: 'the great bulk of the Tulu Brahmins of South Canara adopted the teaching of ... Madhavacharya'.

quote: The Tulu-speaking Brahmins of the present day are almost all followers of Madhavacharya, though a few remain Smarthas
note: Eight Udipi mathas (Sodhe, Krishnapur, Sirur, Kanur, Pejavar, Adamar, Palamar, Puththige), each swami presiding two years in turn over the Krishna temple. A certain number follow the Bhagavat Sampradayam (equal honour to Vishnu and Siva).

quote: The Tulu-speaking Brahmins of the present day are almost all followers of Madhavacharya, though a few remain Smarthas
note: Pitha for the remaining Smartha Tulu Brahmins is Sringeri per the general Tulu statement (see Tulu Brahman general row).

districts_named: Haiga tract (N. Canara and S. Canara); Kasaragod
quote: They did not, like the Shivallis, adopt the teaching of Madhavacharya, but remained followers of Sankaracharya
note: Matha named only in the Saklapuri paragraph ('Ramchandrapura matha'); areca cultivators.

quote: Saklapuris, of whom there are a few in the district, are what may be called a dissenting sect of Havikas who, a few years ago, renounced their allegiance to the Ramchandrapura matha in favour of one at Saklapuri
note: Smarta character inferred from being a sect of Havikas; Thurston/Stuart do not say 'Smarta' of the Saklapuris explicitly.

quote: Kota Brahmins, so called from a village in the northern part of the Udipi taluk, are, like the Haviks, Smarthas or followers of Sankaracharya
note: No matha named for Kotas.

quote: The Oriya Brahmans are both Smarthas and Vaishnavas who are generally Paramarthos or followers of Chaitanya.
note: Intermarriage between Smartha and Paramartho Oriya Brahmans allowed. Jagannatha of Puri reverenced.

quote: All caste disputes are referred to their high priest, the Swamiyar of Kasi Mutt, who resides at Mancheswaram or Basroor.
note: 'A large majority of the Konkani Brahmans are Madhvas'; Cochin Census 1901: 'followers of Madhavacharya'; Venkataramana temples.

quote: the Desasthas are Marathi-speaking Brahmans, who have adopted some of the customs of the Smartha and Madhva Carnatakas, with whom intermarriage is permitted.
note: Customs borrowed; own sect not stated.
